items.headline: adidas makes a chocolate-brown Samba
items.caption: Coffee brown with pale blue stripes and a giant fold-over tongue.
body: The Samba LT W gets a deep brown upper, a nice break from black and white.
The oversized tongue covers much of the top of the shoe.
How to wear it: cream trousers and a navy knit.

items.headline: Asics × Soshiotsuki: only 50 pairs
items.caption: A Skyhand OG in Chromexcel leather shaped by Japanese artisans.
body: It takes the slim, flat-soled sneaker everyone wants and makes it ultra rare.
Japanese craftspeople custom-shape the leather.
How to wear it: if you get a pair, with tailored trousers.

items.headline: FreshService makes high-tech puffers for normal people
items.caption: Light, warm Pertex Quantum pieces from the Japanese brand.
body: FreshService is like an alt version of Muji, with realistic gear for annoying weather.
Blue and grey puffers come with matching hats, scarves and bags.
How to wear it: a light puffer under a long coat on cold days.

items.headline: Nike's oldest sneaker returns in grey
items.caption: The Moon Shoe, Nike's very first, in 'Grey Fog'.
body: Bill Bowerman made the Moon Shoe before Nike was even Nike.
This version comes in soft grey tones.
How to wear it: grey on grey, sweats to suits.

items.headline: Our Legacy teams up with Nike
items.caption: The long-rumoured partnership starts with a vintage Nike pop-up.
body: Our Legacy co-founder Jockum Hallin says the work will 'look slow but feel fast'.
It follows the Swedish label's long Converse collaboration.
How to wear it: Our Legacy's relaxed tailoring with old-school runners.

items.headline: Purple is this season's colour
items.caption: It was all over the autumn/winter runways, and it's easier to wear than you think.
body: Purple has moved from statement shade to everyday colour.
It works with more of your wardrobe than you'd expect.
How to wear it: a plum knit with grey trousers.

items.headline: Which winter jacket person are you?
items.caption: Picking a coat is like picking a car, says Highsnobiety's shopping editor.
body: Many down jackets look alike apart from the logo.
Think about design, not just brand loyalty.
How to wear it: choose the coat for your actual commute.

items.headline: Wales Bonner × adidas is still the best collab
items.caption: Six years in, Grace Wales Bonner's adidas line keeps delivering.
body: Wales Bonner is also the new menswear creative director at Hermès, the first Black woman to lead a European luxury house.
Her first Hermès collection debuts in Paris in January.
How to wear it: a track top over a crisp shirt.

items.headline: Stylish boots for rainy days
items.caption: Seven boots that handle wet weather without looking like rain boots.
body: Skip clunky rubber wellies when it's only drizzling.
Plenty of smart boots handle some rain fine.
How to wear it: dark leather boots with wool trousers; just avoid deep puddles.

items.headline: A film celebrates the first woman to play pro football
items.caption: In 1970, teacher Pat Palinkas played for the Orlando Panthers.
body: She made national headlines, then the world forgot.
Filmmaker Ashley Brandon's 12-minute documentary 'Panther Pat' tells her story.
It mixes interviews with Palinkas and archive footage.

items.headline: Students rebuild a car for a disabled veteran
items.caption: A refurbished Hyundai Elantra gives a Navy veteran his independence back.
body: Robert Hanson hadn't had a car for over two years and struggles with public transport due to health issues.
Students at Dunwoody College of Engineering refurbished the car through a donation program.
He received it in Minneapolis.

items.headline: Birdwatching may help keep your brain young
items.caption: Expert birdwatchers showed brain changes that could slow age-related decline.
body: Researchers looked at how identifying birds keeps the brain adaptable.
Even older birders showed more structural complexity in several brain regions.
Binoculars: the new brain gym.
